title: The effect of the MLB pitch clock
text:
The introduction of the MLB pitch clock was perhaps the most drastic and immediate rule change baseball had seen in decades. The rule change happened after the 2022 baseball season so the first season that had the pitch clock was 2023. The clock fundamentally altered the game’s famous slow cadence. Players, long accustomed to leisurely pacing and endless adjustments on the mound, were now forced into constant motion, transforming a sport once defined by patience into one defined by urgency. This single device, ticking down the seconds, did what years of debate could not. The overall goal, make the game sped up so fans pay more attention. But, someone has to have success off the rule change. Has the batter or pitcher been affected by the pitch clock chnage more?
To determine how overall offensive efficiency has shifted, I looked at the league-wide batting splits over the last 6 seasons, to know if there was a batter advantage after the rule changed.

# Filter and select data
obp <- MLB |> 
  filter(Year >= 2020 & Year <= 2025) |> 
  select(Year, OBP)

slg <- MLB |> 
  filter(Year >= 2020 & Year <= 2025) |> 
  select(Year, SLG)

ops <- MLB |> 
  filter(Year >= 2020 & Year <= 2025) |> 
  select(Year, OPS)

# Combine all three stats into one dataset
MLB_stats <- MLB |> 
  filter(Year >= 2020 & Year <= 2025) |> 
  select(Year, OBP, SLG, OPS) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(OBP, SLG, OPS),
               names_to = "Statistic",
               values_to = "Value")

# Create grouped bar chart
ggplot(MLB_stats, aes(x = factor(Year), y = Value, fill = Statistic)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey", "black", "red")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 0.8, 0.1),  
    limits = c(0, 0.8)
  )+
  labs(
    title = "MLB Offensive Metrics by Year (2020–2025)",
    subtitle= "bfuebeu",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Value",
    fill = "Statistic"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
